title: The article discusses the political landscape in Zimbabwe, focusing on the ZANU(PF) party and its leader, Robert Mugabe, as they face challenges from the opposition party ZAPU. Following Mugabe's appointment as governor, armed ZANU(PF) youths began to patrol with police, indicating a strategy to suppress ZAPU's influence, particularly in the Midlands region. The upcoming ZANU(PF) congress is expected to address internal party tensions, including dissatisfaction with the slow pace of reforms and regional power dynamics. Key figures like Edgar Tekere and Eddison Zvobgo are highlighted as potential challengers to Mugabe's leadership, with speculation about who will fill the vacant secretary-general position. The article suggests that while the party aims to present unity before elections, underlying divisions may emerge afterward, especially given Mugabe's reliance on violence against opposition forces.
